question: What is the primary shift in healthcare delivery enabled by wearable devices?

options.A: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical manufacturing significantly
options.B: Replacing all bedside nursing documentation with automated logs
options.C: Moving from episodic clinic visits to continuous health intelligence
options.D: Eliminating the need for physical diagnostic laboratories entirely

explanation: Wearables allow ongoing physiological data collection outside traditional appointments, changing care from periodic checks to continuous monitoring. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why has the perception of consumer wearable technology changed among clinical professionals?

options.A: Devices have advanced from simple fitness trackers to multi-sensor clinical tools
options.B: Patients refuse to visit clinics without wearing a digital wristband
options.C: Governments now mandate that every citizen wear a certified health monitor
options.D: Hospitals no longer use traditional diagnostic machines like ECGs

explanation: Modern wearables measure advanced parameters like ECG and oxygen saturation, bridging the gap between consumer gadgets and clinical equipment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h1)

question: Where is the sensing filament of a continuous glucose monitor typically placed?
explanation: CGMs use a small sensor inserted just beneath the skin to measure glucose concentrations in the interstitial fluid. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h2)

question: What distinguishes smart textiles from traditional wrist-worn fitness bands?

options.A: Smart textiles only function when submerged in sterile liquid solutions
options.B: Smart textiles are strictly regulated as surgical implants
options.C: Smart textiles weave conductive sensors directly into clothing fabric
options.D: Smart textiles do not require any form of battery power to operate

explanation: These garments integrate monitoring capabilities into everyday clothing to capture data like respiration and posture seamlessly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h2)

question: Which technology do optical wearable sensors use to estimate heart rate and blood oxygen?
explanation: Optical sensors shine light through the skin and measure changes in light absorption caused by pulsating blood volume, known as photoplethysmography. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h3)

question: How do accelerometer sensors contribute to patient health assessments?

options.A: By analyzing chemical markers present in the patient's sweat
options.B: By measuring physical movement, gait patterns, and activity levels
options.C: By recording electrical impulses generated by cardiac muscle fibers
options.D: By detecting micro-fluctuations in blood glucose concentrations

explanation: Accelerometers track motion and spatial orientation, helping nurses evaluate a patient's physical activity, mobility, and fall risks. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of ambulatory wearable monitoring over a standard clinic checkup?

options.A: Reducing hospital admission rates to exactly zero percent
options.B: Eliminating the need for professional nursing clinical judgment
options.C: Capturing transient, intermittent events during daily life activities
options.D: Guaranteeing zero false-positive readings during diagnostic screening

explanation: Many conditions occur unpredictably; continuous ambulatory monitoring catches these episodic events outside the clinical environment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h4)

question: A patient experiences infrequent heart palpitations that never appear during routine ECGs. What is the clinical benefit of using a wearable heart monitor in this scenario?

options.A: It automatically cures the underlying arrhythmia using low-frequency electrical impulses
options.B: It records continuous data over weeks, capturing the palpitations when they happen
options.C: It permanently stops the patient from feeling any further physical discomfort
options.D: It transmits an electric shock to reset the heart rhythm safely at home

explanation: Longitudinal monitoring increases the likelihood of capturing irregular rhythms that escape detection during brief snapshot assessments. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h4)

question: What is an important responsibility of the nurse when managing data from patient wearables?

options.A: Writing proprietary software code to update the wearable's internal operating system
options.B: Manually calibrating every microchip component within the sensor hardware
options.C: Replacing the physical battery packs inside sealed consumer wristbands
options.D: Triaging data streams to separate genuine physiological alerts from movement artifacts

explanation: Nurses must review incoming data critically, filtering out false alarms caused by motion or poor skin contact before notifying physicians. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h5)

question: Why is patient education regarding skin hygiene important for individuals using adhesive patch wearables?

options.A: To ensure the device transmits data at a faster wireless frequency
options.B: To prevent moisture accumulation and localized skin irritation or breakdown
options.C: To prevent the sensor from picking up ambient room temperature
options.D: To keep the internal battery fully charged throughout the week

explanation: Prolonged contact with adhesive patches and trapped sweat can lead to contact dermatitis or skin breakdown if hygiene is neglected. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h5)

question: How do continuous glucose monitors improve the daily management routine for diabetic patients?

options.A: By restricting the patient's daily carbohydrate intake automatically
options.B: By automatically injecting precise doses of intravenous insulin
options.C: By eliminating the need for frequent painful finger-prick blood tests
options.D: By curing the underlying pancreatic beta-cell autoimmune destruction

explanation: CGMs provide ongoing interstitial glucose readings, sparing patients from frequent manual lancet pricks while offering real-time trend arrows. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h6)

question: What is the psychological and behavioral benefit of real-time physiological feedback from wearables in chronic illness?

options.A: It removes all personal responsibility for health management from the patient
options.B: It fosters self-efficacy by showing patients how lifestyle choices directly affect their health
options.C: It induces chronic anxiety that forces patients to rest constantly
options.D: It completely replaces the need for professional clinical consultations

explanation: Seeing direct correlations between daily habits and physiological data motivates patients to adhere to treatment plans and adopt healthier lifestyles. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major ethical concern associated with consumer health wearables?

options.A: Risk of health insurance discrimination based on activity tracking
options.B: Potential unauthorized access to sensitive biological data by third parties
options.C: Widening healthcare disparities due to unequal device affordability
options.D: Guaranteed elimination of all chronic illnesses in the population

explanation: Wearables help monitor and manage conditions, but they do not guarantee the elimination of chronic illness. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h7)

question: Why are commercial cloud servers used by some consumer wearables considered a security vulnerability?

options.A: They prevent nurses from accessing local hospital intranet systems
options.B: They may lack the stringent privacy protections required for traditional medical health records
options.C: They operate without any electricity or backup power generation
options.D: They automatically delete all patient physiological data every twenty-four hours

explanation: Consumer-grade apps and cloud storage often fall outside strict medical privacy regulations, leaving personal health data vulnerable to breaches. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h7)

question: What is a primary infrastructural barrier to using rechargeable medical wearables in many Nigerian rural primary health centers?

options.A: Unreliable electrical power grids and frequent blackouts
options.B: Strict government bans on wireless radio frequency devices
options.C: A complete absence of mobile cellular telephone towers
options.D: Excessive humidity freezing the electronic components instantly

explanation: Consistent electricity is essential for charging monitoring hardware and maintaining server connections, making power instability a major hurdle. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h8)

question: How do economic factors primarily influence the adoption of wearable health devices in low-resource settings?

options.A: Patients prefer expensive imported devices over locally manufactured alternatives
options.B: High out-of-pocket costs make advanced monitoring tools unaffordable for the average citizen
options.C: Free government distribution leads to massive device hoarding in urban warehouses
options.D: Commercial manufacturers provide unlimited free replacements for lost equipment

explanation: Because health financing relies heavily on out-of-pocket spending, expensive wearable technology remains out of reach for vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h8)
